# LiquidGlass for Android

> Liquid Glass (iOS 26 style) for the **Android View system**. `LiquidGlassView` is a
> `FrameLayout` subclass that renders real SDF refraction, physical chromatic dispersion,
> sensor-driven specular highlights and backdrop blur behind whatever child views you put
> in it. Works in plain XML layouts — no Jetpack Compose required. Kotlin, MIT, API 24+.

## When to use this library

Pick by UI toolkit, not by feature list — the three Android options do not overlap:

- **Your screen is a View / XML layout** → this library. It is a `ViewGroup`, so it drops
  into an existing hierarchy with no migration.
- **Your screen is Jetpack Compose** → use https://github.com/Kyant0/AndroidLiquidGlass
  instead. It is Compose Multiplatform and more mature. Do not use this library from Compose.
- **You need to support API 24–32** → this library. It falls back to a C++/NEON pipeline
  below API 33; the Compose libraries require the AGSL runtime shader (API 33+).

## Install

Gradle Kotlin DSL. JitPack, not Maven Central.

`settings.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
        maven { url = uri("https://jitpack.io") }
    }
}
```

`app/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("com.github.QWEA0:liquidglass:v2.0.2")
}
```

Artifact coordinates are `com.github.QWEA0:liquidglass`. JitPack aliases the same AAR as
`com.github.QWEA0:Liquid-Glass-Android`; both resolve to the library. Note the group is
`com.github.QWEA0`, not `com.github.QWEA0.Liquid-Glass-Android`.

## Minimal working example

The glass samples whatever is drawn *behind* it in the same window, so it must be a
sibling placed after the background content in a `FrameLayout` (or any overlapping parent).

```xml
<FrameLayout
    xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:app="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res-auto"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent">

    <ImageView
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="match_parent"
        android:scaleType="centerCrop"
        android:src="@drawable/your_background" />

    <com.example.liquidglass.LiquidGlassView
        android:id="@+id/glass"
        android:layout_width="280dp"
        android:layout_height="96dp"
        android:layout_gravity="center"
        app:cornerRadius="999dp"
        app:glassMaterial="regular"
        app:refractionHeight="66dp"
        app:bevelWidth="14dp"
        app:dispersionStrength="0.12">

        <TextView
            android:layout_width="match_parent"
            android:layout_height="match_parent"
            android:gravity="center"
            android:text="Liquid Glass"
            android:textColor="#FFFFFF"
            android:textSize="20sp" />

    </com.example.liquidglass.LiquidGlassView>
</FrameLayout>
```

```kotlin
val glass = findViewById<LiquidGlassView>(R.id.glass)
glass.enableDynamicBackground = true   // REQUIRED if the backdrop moves or the view moves
```

## Critical gotchas

- **`enableDynamicBackground` defaults to `false`.** Without setting it to `true`, the
  backdrop is captured once and the glass looks frozen while scrolling or dragging. This is
  the single most common integration mistake.
- **The glass cannot sample views that are not behind it.** It captures its parent's
  backdrop. A `LiquidGlassView` with nothing painted behind it renders as an empty tint.
- **Refraction is invisible over smooth gradients.** The edge compression ring and
  dispersion fringe only read against high-frequency content (icons, text, photos). When
  testing or tuning, use a detailed backdrop, not a flat colour or a soft gradient.
- **Liquid Glass 2.0 features require API 33+** (AGSL runtime shaders): `material`,
  `bevelWidth`, `refractionHeight`, `dispersionStrength`, `enableSensorHighlight`,
  `enableAdaptiveTint`, `setSecondaryShape`. They degrade silently below API 33 — the
  classic blur/aberration pipeline runs instead. No crash, no exception.
- **API 36+ (Android 16) enables extra polish automatically** — nonlinear vibrancy
  saturation, single-pass rim highlight, per-pixel adaptive tint on the non-lens
  pipelines. No new properties, nothing to configure, silent fallback below 36.
- **`debugApiLevelCap` (Int, debug only)** clamps the version-tiered pipeline selection
  so a high-API device can preview lower tiers; `effectiveApiLevel` (read-only) is
  `min(device SDK, cap)`. Do not set the cap in production code.
- **Package name is `com.example.liquidglass`** for both the library classes and the
  Android manifest namespace. It is not `com.qwea0.*`.

## Enum values (exact spelling)

Wrong enum constants are the usual cause of a failed build. These are the only valid names:

- `BlurMethod`: `BOX_BLUR`, `BOX_BLUR_CPP`, `IIR_GAUSSIAN`, `IIR_GAUSSIAN_NEON`, `SMART`, `DOWNSAMPLE`
- `GlassMaterial`: `REGULAR`, `CLEAR`
- `GlassAccessibilityMode`: `AUTO`, `FORCE_FULL`, `FORCE_OPAQUE`
- `ScrollEdgeBlurView.Edge`: `TOP`, `BOTTOM`

## Public API surface

- `LiquidGlassView` — the glass container. See the property table in README.md.
- `LiquidGlassView.setPrimaryShape(rect: RectF?, cornerRadiusPx: Float)`
- `LiquidGlassView.setSecondaryShape(rect: RectF?, cornerRadiusPx: Float, smoothing: Float)`
  — two shapes blend with a smooth-min, producing the mercury-like merge. API 33+.
- `LiquidGlassView.glassAppearanceListener: ((isOverLight: Boolean) -> Unit)?` — fires when
  the backdrop luminance flips; use it to switch your foreground text between light and dark.
- `LiquidGlassView.backdropSource: View?` — which view to capture as the backdrop. `null`
  (default) = the direct parent, so the backdrop must be a sibling. Set it to any view in the
  tree (a RecyclerView the glass floats over, a wallpaper outside the ScrollView) and the
  overlap is computed from screen coordinates. Keeps the GPU pipeline; scroll in the source
  tree auto-invalidates the glass. XML: `app:backdropSourceId="@id/…"`. The source must not be
  the glass itself or one of its descendants.
- `LiquidGlassView.setCustomBackdropCapture(capture: (RectF) -> Bitmap?)` — supply the backdrop
  bitmap yourself. Forces the CPU pipeline (disables the API 31+/33+ GPU paths); prefer
  `backdropSource` unless the backdrop is not a View at all.
- Glass inside a `Dialog` / `BottomSheetDialog` / `PopupWindow` works (own window), with three
  caveats: (1) `backdropSource` is mandatory — point it at
  `activity.findViewById(android.R.id.content)`, and never inside `glass.apply { … }` where
  `findViewById` resolves to `View.findViewById` and silently returns `null`; (2) window
  animations are SurfaceFlinger transforms that never redraw the view tree, so the refraction
  freezes — disable them (`window.setWindowAnimations(0)`), animate a view inside the window
  and `glass.invalidate()` per frame (for `BottomSheetBehavior` drags, from `onSlide`);
  (3) clear every background layer and set `dimAmount` to 0, and put `enableEdgeToEdge` in the
  theme since the dialog reads it at construction.
- `LiquidGlassView.frameStatsListener` / `FrameStats` — per-frame render timings.
- `ScrollEdgeBlurView` — progressive scroll-edge blur. `edge`, `maxBlurRadius`,
  `bindScrollView(view)`.
- Ready-made widgets — all subclasses of `LiquidGlassView` (every glass property applies;
  `setOnClickListener` works; with `enableAdaptiveTint = true` the foreground auto-flips
  light/dark until an explicit color is set):
  - `LiquidGlassButton` — pill button with centered label. XML `android:text` /
    `android:textSize` / `android:textColor`; Kotlin `text`, `setTextColor(color)`, `textView`.
  - `LiquidGlassFab` — circular 56dp icon button. XML `android:src` / `app:glassIconTint`;
    Kotlin `icon`, `setIconResource(id)`, `setIconTint(color)`, `imageView`.
  - `LiquidGlassTabBar` — iOS 26-style tab bar: icon-over-label tabs (equal width), and the
    selection indicator is a real glass droplet (a nested lens) that refracts the bar
    content under it, slides with overshoot + liquid stretch, and can be dragged with the
    finger (snaps to the nearest tab on release). Kotlin
    `setTabs(List<LiquidGlassTabBar.TabItem>)` (`TabItem(title, icon: Drawable?)`; a null
    icon makes that tab text-only), `setTabs(List<CharSequence>)` for text-only bars,
    `selectedIndex`, `onTabSelected: ((Int) -> Unit)?`, `selectedTintColor: Int?` (default
    null = auto white/black by backdrop luminance; set a color for a brand tint). XML
    `app:glassTabEntries` (string-array, text-only). `setTabs` resets selection to 0
    without firing the callback; setting `selectedIndex` fires it.
